```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`select_clips()` offers three sampling designs, set by `sampling_mode`.
They answer different questions, and a validation sample drawn for one
purpose is generally not valid for another. This vignette states what each
design is for, runs the three on the example data shipped with the package
and compares the clips they select.

| `sampling_mode` | unit drawn | selection | use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"top"` | prediction | highest confidence per stratum | classifier retraining; score-to-probability calibration |
| `"random_detections"` | occasion with a detection | random, within score-independent strata | false-positive rates, observation-confirmation design |
| `"random_recordings"` | recording or minute | random, among all recorded | false-positive and false-negative rates, multiple-method design |

## Example data

The example consists of simulated BirdNET selection tables (Raven format)
of anuran calls at several sites over six months (October 2021 to March
2022), plus the list of every recording made (`recordings.csv`),
including those without any prediction. The audio files do not exist:
`Begin Path` points to a fictitious network drive. Because `select_clips()`
never reads audio, this does not prevent any of the steps below.

```{r}
library(sheepdog)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

ex   <- system.file("extdata", "example", package = "sheepdog")
pred <- suppressMessages(read_selection_tables(file.path(ex, "birdnet")))
recs <- readr::read_csv(file.path(ex, "recordings.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)
count(pred, site)
```

There are `r nrow(pred)` predictions of `r n_distinct(pred$species_code)` species at
`r n_distinct(pred$site)` sites, from `r nrow(recs)` recordings of 300 s. Recording effort
differs among sites:

```{r}
count(recs, site, name = "recordings")
```

Throughout, the occupancy analysis is assumed to treat a
prediction with confidence $\geq$ 0.5 as a detection:

```{r}
threshold <- 0.5
above <- filter(pred, confidence >= threshold)
nrow(above)
```

## `"top"`: the highest scores

`"top"` keeps the `n_top` predictions with the highest confidence in each
site × species × night × hour stratum. Predictions below `min_confidence`
are discarded first.

```{r}
top <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "top", n_top = 1,
                    min_confidence = threshold)
```

This design is appropriate for two purposes. First, retraining the
classifier, where confirmed high-score examples of each species are the
most useful additions to the training set. Second, the
score-to-probability calibration of `calibrate()`: the calibration model
describes the probability that a prediction is correct *conditional on its
score*, so selecting clips by score does not bias it, provided the
selected clips span the range of scores of interest.

`"top"` is not a probability sample, and `inclusion_prob` is `NA`. It must
not be used to estimate false-positive rates for occupancy models. Clips
with the highest scores contain fewer false positives than a random sample
of detections, so the proportion of negatives among them underestimates the
false-positive rate of the detections that enter the detection history.

## `"random_detections"`: observation-confirmation design

In the observation-confirmation design (Chambert et al. 2015), a random
subset of the occasions with a detection is checked, and every detection of
a checked occasion is confirmed or rejected. `"random_detections"`
implements it as follows:

1. A candidate occasion is an occasion with at least one prediction of the
   species with confidence $\geq$ `threshold`. The occasion is the sampling
   unit of the occupancy model, set by `occasion_unit`: the whole recording
   (`"file"`) or one minute of it (`"minute"`).
2. `n_top` candidate occasions are drawn at random in each site × species ×
   night × hour stratum. The strata do not depend on the score, so every
   detection has a known, non-zero probability of being checked.
3. Every prediction $\geq$ `threshold` of a drawn occasion becomes a clip.

`threshold` is required and must equal the threshold of the occupancy
analysis; otherwise the occasions drawn are not the occasions scored as
detections in the model.

With `occasion_unit = "file"`:

```{r}
rd_file <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_detections",
                        occasion_unit = "file", threshold = threshold,
                        n_top = 1)
table(rd_file$inclusion_prob)

files_per_stratum <- recs |>
  mutate(stamp = sub(".*_(\\d{8})_(\\d{2}).*", "\\1_\\2", source_audio)) |>
  count(site, stamp)
max(files_per_stratum$n)
```

In the example data each site × night × hour holds at most
`r max(files_per_stratum$n)` recording, so each stratum contains at most one candidate file and the first-stage draw
keeps all of them (`inclusion_prob` = 1). The same applies to any recording
schedule with one file per hour. Subsampling then requires a coarser
stratum, minute occasions or the limits described under
[Limiting the effort](#limiting-the-effort).

The `strata` argument sets the stratum of the draw: `"night_hour"` (the
default), `"night"` or `"site_species"`. With `strata = "night"`, the
files of a night compete with each other, and one is drawn per site ×
species × night:

```{r}
rd_night <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_detections",
                         occasion_unit = "file", threshold = threshold,
                         n_top = 1, strata = "night")
summary(rd_night$inclusion_prob)
```

Besides `"night_hour"`, `"night"` and `"site_species"`, the presets
`"hour"` (pooling the nights), `"week"` and `"month"` spread the draw
over the diel cycle or the season. With `strata = "month"`, the files
of a month compete with each other:

```{r}
rd_month <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_detections",
                         occasion_unit = "file", threshold = threshold,
                         n_top = 2, strata = "month")
summary(rd_month$inclusion_prob)
```

`strata` also takes a vector of column names, for strata defined by the
user. Any column added to the predictions before the call can be used.
Since site and species are always part of the strata, a useful column
varies within a site: the rain of the night, a recorder when a site has
several, or, as here, the moon phase, approximated from the date of the
night (days since a reference new moon, modulo the synodic month of
29.53 days) and crossed with the month.

```{r}
moon_phase <- function(night) {
  days <- as.numeric(as.Date(night, "%Y%m%d") - as.Date("2000-01-06"))
  cut(days %% 29.530588, breaks = c(0, 7.38, 14.77, 22.15, 29.54),
      labels = c("new", "first_quarter", "full", "last_quarter"),
      include.lowest = TRUE)
}
# the date (YYYYMMDD) comes from the name of the recording
rd_moon <- pred |>
  mutate(date = regmatches(begin_path, regexpr("\\d{8}(?=_\\d{6})",
                                                begin_path, perl = TRUE)),
         moon = as.character(moon_phase(date))) |>
  select_clips(sampling_mode = "random_detections", occasion_unit = "file",
               threshold = threshold, n_top = 1,
               strata = c("month", "moon"))
rd_moon |>
  distinct(site, species_code, occasion_id) |>
  nrow()
```

`site` and `species_code` are always part of the strata, so that
`inclusion_prob` stays exact when `target_total` or `max_per_species`
draw again within site × species. The strata must not depend on the
score: `select_clips()` refuses `confidence` and `rank`, and every stratum
column must be constant within an occasion. Any stratum that meets these
conditions is compatible with the observation-confirmation design.

With `occasion_unit = "minute"`, a stratum holds up to five candidate
minutes per recording, and one is drawn:

```{r}
rd <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_detections",
                   occasion_unit = "minute", threshold = threshold,
                   n_top = 1)
```

`occasion_id` identifies the occasion, `n_detections_occasion` counts the
predictions $\geq$ `threshold` of the species in it, and `inclusion_prob` is
the probability that the occasion was drawn:

```{r}
rd |>
  select(site, species_code, occasion_id, rank, confidence,
         n_detections_occasion, inclusion_prob) |>
  head(4)
count(rd, inclusion_prob)
```

`inclusion_prob` is $\min(n_\mathrm{top}, N) / N$, where $N$ is the number of
candidate occasions in the stratum. Because every detection of a drawn
occasion is cut, the number of clips per occasion equals
`n_detections_occasion`:

```{r}
per_occasion <- count(rd, site, species_code, occasion_id,
                      n_detections_occasion, name = "n_clips")
all(per_occasion$n_clips == per_occasion$n_detections_occasion)
```

This check is worth repeating on the validation table before passing it to
an occupancy model: a clip missing from an occasion breaks the assumption
that all of its detections were confirmed.

## `"random_recordings"`: multiple-method design

In the multiple-method design (Miller et al. 2011), a second, unambiguous
method (here, annotation by ear of whole recordings) is applied to a random
subset of the sampling units, irrespective of whether the classifier
detected anything. This provides information on false negatives as well as
false positives. `"random_recordings"` draws recordings (or minutes, with
`occasion_unit = "minute"`) among all those recorded, with or without
predictions, in proportion to the effort at each site: `recording_fraction`
of the recordings of each site, or a fixed `n_recordings_per_site`.

The draw needs the list of every recording. By default it is obtained by
listing the audio folders that appear in `Begin Path`, which omits folders
without any prediction and fails here because the audio files do not exist.
The `recordings` argument supplies the list instead:

```{r}
rr <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_recordings",
                   recordings = file.path(ex, "recordings.csv"),
                   recording_fraction = 0.1, recording_duration = 300,
                   species = "boa-ran")
rr |>
  select(site, species_code, clip_file, clip_start, clip_end,
         confidence, inclusion_prob) |>
  head(3)
count(rr, site)
```

The number drawn per site follows its recording effort: with
`recording_fraction = 0.1`, the site with the fewest recordings
(`r names(which.min(table(recs$site)))`, `r min(table(recs$site))`) contributes
`r min(table(rr$site))` recordings, and `inclusion_prob` is the fraction drawn at
that site. The default `recording_fraction = 0.01` suits large projects: with
fewer than 150 recordings per site it draws a single recording per site,
so small projects should raise it or set `n_recordings_per_site`.

Each clip is a whole recording (or minute); `confidence` is `NA` and `rank`
is `NA`. `recording_duration` sets `clip_end`; without it, `clip_end` is
`NA` for whole recordings and minute occasions require reading the files
with the 'av' package. The recording is copied once per species to annotate,
so that each copy receives a verdict for one species in that species'
folder. Without `species`, every species with predictions is included, which
multiplies the listening effort by the number of species:

```{r}
rr_all <- suppressMessages(
  select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_recordings",
               recordings = file.path(ex, "recordings.csv"),
               recording_fraction = 0.1, recording_duration = 300)
)
c(recordings = n_distinct(rr_all$occasion_id), clips = nrow(rr_all))
```

Restrict `species` to the species that will actually be annotated.
Recordings of `"random_recordings"` are not confirmations of detections and
are handled differently downstream (see `vignette("crywolf-integration")`).

## Comparing the selected scores

The practical difference between `"top"` and `"random_detections"` is
visible in the confidence of the clips they select. The reference is the
distribution of all predictions $\geq$ `threshold`, i.e. the detections that
enter the detection history. Clips from `"random_detections"` are weighted
by `1 / inclusion_prob` (design weights), because occasions in strata with
many candidates have a lower probability of being drawn.

```{r}
wquantile <- function(x, w = rep(1, length(x)),
                      probs = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9)) {
  o  <- order(x)
  cw <- cumsum(w[o]) / sum(w)
  setNames(x[o][vapply(probs, \(p) which(cw >= p)[1], integer(1))],
           paste0(probs * 100, "%"))
}

score_quantiles <- rbind(
  `all >= threshold`  = wquantile(above$confidence),
  random_detections   = wquantile(rd$confidence, 1 / rd$inclusion_prob),
  top                 = wquantile(top$confidence)
)
round(score_quantiles, 3)
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
q <- round(score_quantiles, 2)
```

The weighted quantiles of `"random_detections"` track those of all
detections (median `r q["random_detections", "50%"]` against
`r q["all >= threshold", "50%"]`), whereas `"top"` is shifted upwards
(median `r q["top", "50%"]`). To the extent that false positives receive lower
scores than true detections, as they do on average in the simulated data
(although the two distributions overlap), a false-positive rate estimated
from the `"top"` clips is biased low.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5, fig.alt = "Empirical cumulative distribution of confidence for all detections, random_detections clips and top clips."}
library(ggplot2)

wecdf <- function(x, w, design) {
  o <- order(x)
  tibble(confidence = x[o], ecdf = cumsum(w[o]) / sum(w), design = design)
}
curves <- bind_rows(
  wecdf(above$confidence, rep(1, nrow(above)), "all >= threshold"),
  wecdf(rd$confidence, 1 / rd$inclusion_prob, "random_detections"),
  wecdf(top$confidence, rep(1, nrow(top)), "top")
)

ggplot(curves, aes(confidence, ecdf, colour = design)) +
  geom_step() +
  labs(x = "Confidence", y = "Cumulative proportion", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Limiting the effort {#limiting-the-effort}

`target_total`, `max_per_species` and `balance_by_hour` cap the number of
units to review after the stratified draw. Their effect differs among
designs:

- `target_total` sets the total per site, split evenly among species by
  water filling (species with fewer units than their share enter whole, and
  the surplus goes to the others). In `"top"` it counts clips; in
  `"random_detections"` it counts occasions, each of which may yield
  several clips.
- `max_per_species` sets a fixed limit per site × species. It is ignored
  when `target_total` is set.
- `balance_by_hour = TRUE` draws round-robin across the hours of the day
  within each species, so that the reviewed sample covers the diel cycle.
- In `"random_recordings"` the effort is set by `recording_fraction` or
  `n_recordings_per_site`; `target_total` and `max_per_species` are ignored
  with a warning.

```{r}
target <- 40
top_cap <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "top", n_top = 1,
                        min_confidence = threshold, target_total = target)
rd_cap  <- select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_detections",
                        occasion_unit = "minute", threshold = threshold,
                        n_top = 1, target_total = target)
```

```{r}
rd_cap |>
  distinct(site, species_code, occasion_id) |>
  count(site, name = "occasions") |>
  left_join(count(rd_cap, site, name = "clips"), by = "site") |>
  left_join(count(top_cap, site, name = "top_clips"), by = "site")
```

The same target of `r target` units per site yields `r nrow(top_cap)` clips in
`"top"` but `r nrow(rd_cap)` clips in `"random_detections"` (`r n_distinct(pred$site)` sites), because every
detection of a drawn occasion must be reviewed. Plan the target in occasions
and expect a larger number of clips.

The second-stage draw enters `inclusion_prob`, which is the product of the
first-stage probability and the fraction of candidate occasions kept in the
stratum (site × species, and hour when `balance_by_hour = TRUE`):

```{r}
summary(rd_cap$inclusion_prob)
```

Because the target is split evenly among species, rare species have higher
inclusion probabilities than common ones: the unweighted pool of clips
over-represents them, and estimates pooled across species must weight the
clips by `1 / inclusion_prob`.

In `"random_recordings"` the cap is not applied:

```{r}
tryCatch(
  select_clips(pred, sampling_mode = "random_recordings",
               recordings = file.path(ex, "recordings.csv"),
               recording_duration = 300, target_total = target),
  warning = \(w) conditionMessage(w)
)
```

## Sensors that discard the audio

Some recorders now run the classifier on the device and keep only the
detections, discarding the audio to save storage or transmission. No clip
can then be reviewed, and none of the designs above can be applied after
the fact: the calibration and the false-positive rate of an occupancy model
both need verified clips drawn with a known probability. The remedy is a
design decision taken before deployment: keep a probability sample of the
raw audio, drawn without looking at the scores, e.g. one recording in a
hundred at random in each site, or a fixed random subset of the recording
schedule. Those recordings can later be annotated by ear, as in
`"random_recordings"`, and their detections reviewed, as in
`"random_detections"`. Keeping only the audio of high-score detections, or of
detections the device found ambiguous, is not a substitute: such a sample
depends on the scores, like `"top"`, and cannot estimate the false-positive
rate.

## Hand-off to occupancy models

The manifest returned by `select_clips()` is cut with `cut_clips()` (or in
one step with `extract_validation_clips()`), reviewed, and joined to the
verdicts with `post_validation()`. The columns that occupancy models with
false positives read (`occasion_id`, `n_detections_occasion`,
`inclusion_prob`, `verdict`), and how clips of each design must be used, are
defined in `vignette("crywolf-integration")`.

## References

Chambert, T., Miller, D. A. W., & Nichols, J. D. (2015). Modeling false
positive detections in species occurrence data under different study
designs. *Ecology*, 96, 332–339. <https://doi.org/10.1890/14-1507.1>

Miller, D. A., Nichols, J. D., McClintock, B. T., Grant, E. H. C., Bailey,
L. L., & Weir, L. A. (2011). Improving occupancy estimation when two types
of observational error occur: non-detection and species misidentification.
*Ecology*, 92, 1422–1428. <https://doi.org/10.1890/10-1396.1>
